svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: impulse from receptor to spinal cord
svg.title: Sensory neuron (longitudinal view)
svg.desc: A pseudounipolar sensory neuron: free nerve endings in the skin, a long myelinated peripheral axon to a T-junction, a short stem process to the cell body in the dorsal root ganglion, and a central axon entering the spinal cord where it ends in synaptic knobs.

g.data-info: The outer layer of skin, where the free nerve endings lie among epidermal cells.
Part of the central nervous system. The central axon enters it through the dorsal root.
A swelling on the dorsal root of a spinal nerve that holds the cell bodies of sensory neurons.

Free nerve endings in the skin. Their membranes contain ion channels that open in response to a stimulus (e.g. heat, pressure, chemicals), depolarising the membrane. If threshold is reached, an action potential starts.

Long fibre carrying impulses from the receptor towards the cell body and spinal cord. In a sensory neuron it is structurally an axon (myelinated, conducts action potentials); older textbooks call it a dendron.
A single short process joins the cell body to the fibre where the peripheral and central processes meet. Impulses usually pass straight through the junction without entering the cell body.

Lies in the dorsal root ganglion, just outside the spinal cord. It has no dendrites (pseudounipolar neuron). It keeps the neuron alive: nucleus, ribosomes and mitochondria make proteins for the whole cell.
Carries the impulse from the T-junction into the spinal cord (central nervous system).
Ends of the central axon inside the spinal cord. They release neurotransmitter onto relay neurons (or directly onto motor neurons in a simple reflex).
Large, round and central, with a prominent nucleolus.
Makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosomes for protein synthesis.
Layers of Schwann cell membrane insulating the axon between the nodes, so the impulse jumps from node to node (saltatory conduction).
Each Schwann cell myelinates one internode of the peripheral nerve fibre; its nucleus lies outside the myelin.
Gap between neighbouring Schwann cells where voltage-gated Na⁺ and K⁺ channels are concentrated and action potentials are regenerated.

svg.text: Not to scale: the fibre (up to about 1 m) is shortened, shown by the break.
